validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate action needed. Row is a real, correctly named, correctly classified trunk (магистральный) gas transmission pipeline, confirmed by two independent, cross-viewpoint sources seven years apart (a 2015 Russian outlet and a 2022 Ukrainian outlet), both naming it by this exact route name and describing damage-repair events on it specifically — not a generic country-level citation. Not a duplicate of any other roster row: no other of the 39 Ukraine-gas rows shares this route (Kramatorsk→Donetsk→Mariupol); P5989 (Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk) is a physically distinct corridor terminating at Berdyansk, not Mariupol.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + NAME + CLASSIFICATION: neftegaz.ru (Russian trade outlet, dated 2015-06-12) reports damage to 'магистральный газопровод (МГП) Ду 1000 Краматорск - Донецк - Мариуполь' (trunk gas pipeline DN1000 Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol), giving a precise damage location (Yasinovataysky district, between Krasnogorovka and Novokalinovo villages, near Ocheretino, NW of Donetsk city) and naming the then-operator Ukrtransgaz (correct for 2015, pre-2020 restructuring — not evidence about the current operator, per country guidance). Independently, biz.liga.net/LIGA.net (Ukrainian outlet, dated 2022-03-06, machine-translated from Ukrainian) reports 'Diskatcher ОГтСУ зафиксировали резкий скачок давления ... газопровода Краматорск-Донецк-Мариуполь' (dispatchers of Gas TSO of Ukraine (OGTSU) recorded a pressure spike indicating damage to the Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol gas pipeline from Russian shelling), naming the current operator by its post-2020 name. These are genuinely independent (different countries, different outlets, seven years apart, opposite editorial viewpoints on the war) and both name this exact pipeline specifically — not a generic Ukraine-GTS citation — so this clears the 2+-independent bar at tier=high for existence, naming, classification as a trunk/transmission line, and Fuel=Gas. The wiki page's other cited refs are weaker/dead and were not used: tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/ is Cloudflare-blocked (403) and is a generic TSO-facts page, not pipeline-specific; nord-stream2.com/en/download/document/80/ no longer resolves at all (DNS failure, domain effectively dead post-2022); novosti.dn.ua's cited article 404s; the LinkedIn 'Gas TSO of Ukraine' company page is generic, not pipeline-specific. None of these were cited.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat StartYear1=1999 as settled. The one dated source found on the construction period says the line was built 1990–1998 (i.e. plausibly completed 1998, a year earlier), and it also gives a distinct 1978 founding date for the Makeevka linear production directorate that historically operated it — a fact that must not be conflated with the pipeline's own build year. Recommend Update search Soviet-era gas-industry engineering literature (per the country source ladder §6) for a primary construction record before changing StartYear1 either way; flagging as an open disagreement rather than proposing a replacement value off a single source.
validity.researcher_notes: neftegaz.ru (2015) states: 'МГП Ду 1000 Краматорск - Донецк - Мариуполь строился в период 1990 - 1998 гг. и до войны относился к Макеевскому линейному производственному управлению магистральных газопроводов (ЛПУМГ), созданному в 1978 г.' (the pipeline was under construction 1990-1998, and before the war belonged to the Makeevka LPUMG, created in 1978). This is one source only for the pipeline's own build period — could not find a second independent source giving a construction/commissioning date, so this is not yet a resolved corroborated finding, just a live disagreement with the sheet's 1999 that Update should chase rather than silently accept. Note the 1978 date in the same sentence is for the operating directorate's founding, not the pipe itself — GEM's StartYear1 should never be backfilled from that number.

fills.researcher_notes: Both articles describe an in-service trunk line being taken offline temporarily for shelling repair (2015) or shelling damage (2022), each event framed as a disruption to a normally-operating asset (2015: ~2-day repair estimate, transit unaffected; 2022: dispatchers detecting a pressure anomaly on an operating system). Status is inferred from context per instructions, not required as a literal token match. No dated evidence of permanent decommissioning found.

Both sources call it газопровод (gas pipeline) throughout and describe natural-gas supply disruptions to downstream cities/gas-distribution stations as the consequence of the damage — fuel is unambiguously natural gas.

Both sources explicitly call it магистральный газопровод (МГП) — trunk/main gas pipeline, the standard Russian/Ukrainian term for a high-pressure transmission trunk as distinct from a gathering or feeder line (газопровод-отвод). The 2022 article's separate mention of a distinct газопровод-отвод (feeder) damaged in Kharkiv Oblast on 2022-03-02 shows the outlet uses the two terms deliberately, not interchangeably — the Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol line is squarely in the trunk/transmission category.

neftegaz.ru states the diameter directly and twice: 'Ду 1000' (диаметр условный / nominal diameter 1000mm), matching the sheet's Diameter=1000/mm exactly. Only one independent source found stating diameter specifically (biz.liga.net does not give a diameter figure) — tier medium, single strong source, not yet the 2-independent bar.

Both sources name the route by exactly this endpoint pair (Kramatorsk→Donetsk→Mariupol) and neftegaz.ru additionally pinpoints a mid-route damage location (Yasinovataysky district, between Krasnogorovka and Novokalinovo, near Ocheretino, NW of Donetsk city) — all inside Donetsk Oblast, consistent with the sheet's start/end oblast values. Mariupol is administratively part of Donetsk Oblast, matching EndState/Province. This confirms the corridor/route naming, not exact endpoint coordinates — no route geometry claim is made here.
